new_findings.expected_impact: Explains 100% of this session's launch failures; blocks everything downstream of import.
new_findings.source: runs/baseline/2fc18296.../server.log; /opt/envs/wu1w/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py:833-860; Magpie/modes/benchmark/benchmarker.py:776,800; reproduced in-session: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -c 'import vllm' -> same RuntimeError
new_findings.what: ROOT CAUSE of the 'unknown' launch failure is NOT a model gap. Magpie composes the server env as os.environ.copy() overlaid with benchmark.envs (_build_local_command, benchmarker.py:776/800). benchmark.envs pins ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 for TP=1 but never HIP/CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, so the harness-inherited PHYSICAL HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES (observed '2' live; '2,3' in the 13:50 baseline log) survives into the vllm child. torch._parse_visible_devices() hard-raises when len(HIP)>len(ROCR), and vLLM triggers it during 'import vllm' (env_override -> torch.cuda.is_available()). The process therefore dies before binding a port, so no model-side error exists to classify -> the empty/unknown failure_kind signature.

new_findings.expected_impact: Explains how an env-only enablement attempt could be integrated and still fail (i.e. a REVERTED prior patch).
new_findings.source: in-session: ROCR=0 HIP=2 -> device_count 1 but is_available False, torch.ones(4,device='cuda') -> 'No CUDA GPUs are available'; ROCR=0 HIP=0 -> count 1, MI250X gfx90a, tensor OK
new_findings.what: Second, SILENT variant of the same bug: equal-count-but-out-of-range masks (ROCR=0 with HIP=2 - the exact leak present in the live coordinator env) do NOT raise; they yield torch.cuda.is_available()==False and 'No CUDA GPUs are available' at first device placement. A fix that merely satisfies torch's length check (pinning HIP to a same-length PHYSICAL id) passes validation and then dies later and less legibly. Only the LOGICAL 0..n-1 index is correct, because ROCR filters at the HSA agent layer and re-indexes what survives.

new_findings.what: A patch against the allowed /opt/envs/vllm/.../vllm/ tree is INERT for this combo: the serving binary is VLLM_BIN=/usr/local/bin/vllm-wu1w -> 'exec /opt/envs/wu1w/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main', which imports vllm+torch from /opt/envs/wu1w - NOT in the allowed source roots (verified: only 3 .py files differ between the two vllm trees, both report 0.28.0). The patchable surface that actually sits on the serving path is Magpie at /opt/envs/vllm/lib/python3.12/site-packages/Magpie (= manifest.dependencies.magpie.path), the layer that composes the crashing env.

new_findings.source: scratch/e2e/magpie.log (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'huggingface_hub'); InferenceX@3d55815/benchmarks/benchmark_lib.sh:682,870,1011 and utils/bench_serving/backend_request_func.py:12; verified /opt/venv/bin/python3 -c 'import huggingface_hub' -> ModuleNotFoundError and /opt/venv/bin/python3 benchmark_serving.py --help -> same crash under the gate PATH
new_findings.what: NEW DEEPER BLOCKER exposed (masked until now because every prior attempt died at the server): the benchmark CLIENT cannot import. benchmark_lib.sh:682 invokes a bare 'python3', which the gate's own PATH resolves to /opt/venv/bin/python3; that interpreter has torch/numpy/aiohttp/tqdm but NOT huggingface_hub or transformers, so utils/bench_serving/backend_request_func.py:12 'import huggingface_hub.constants' aborts with ModuleNotFoundError and no inferencex_result.json is produced. It is a chicken-and-egg gap: the harness's own _install_lm_eval_deps() (which would pull them transitively via lm-eval) is called only from run_eval at benchmark_lib.sh:1011, i.e. AFTER run_benchmark_serving has already died. vllm itself is optional in the client (guarded import), so exactly two pinned packages are missing.

new_findings.expected_impact: Precedent-backed, low-risk shape for the fix.
new_findings.what: The InferenceX launcher already encodes the intended rule (benchmarks/vllm_mi300x.sh:65 derives HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0..n-1 from ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES) but guards it with [ -z "$HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES" ], so it cannot fire for a value inherited from the parent env. The authored patch is that same sanctioned reconciliation moved to the layer that owns the merge - a backport of in-tree behaviour, not a new policy, and it also covers the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES leak (which vLLM's _sync_hip_cuda_env_vars copies onto HIP at import, and a HIP/CUDA disagreement is itself a hard ValueError there).

proposal_set.name: device-mask-logical-reconcile
proposal_set.reason: Belt-and-braces companion to the patch, and the exact configuration PROVEN to boot this session (/health 200 + coherent greedy text on port 8911, and full CUDA-graph capture through the real Magpie path on port 8922). Drops the harness-inherited PHYSICAL mask and re-pins the LOGICAL index that ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 already establishes, so torch never sees HIP count > ROCR count. atomic=true: the three keys are only self-consistent as a set (HIP without ROCR would re-target a physical card). If the patch is kept this variant is a no-op; if the patch is reverted it still unblocks the variant lane. NOTE it cannot fix the baseline - only the patch does that, since the baseline has no server-args/env delta to carry.

summary: Diagnosed the 'unknown' gap as an inherited ROCm device-mask contradiction, not a model gap: the harness leaks a PHYSICAL HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES ('2'), Magpie overlays ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 from the yaml without touching HIP, and torch._parse_visible_devices() then raises inside 'import vllm' - so the server dies before binding a port and nothing model-side is ever reached to classify (hence failure_kind=unknown). Authored a 158-line pure-insertion patch to Magpie's _build_local_command that reconciles HIP/CUDA to the LOGICAL 0..n-1 set ROCR re-indexes to (the rule the InferenceX launcher already states but cannot apply to an inherited value), with vendor guard + fail-open so it is inert on CUDA and on already-valid masks. PROVEN END-TO-END: ran the real Magpie serving path under a deliberately leaked parent env with the patch on PYTHONPATH -> logs 'Device-mask reconciliation for local run: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES: 2 -> 0', weights load, 35/35 CUDA graphs capture, GET /health 200 OK. Cleared the reported launch gap. NEXT DEEPER FAILURE now exposed: the bench CLIENT interpreter /opt/venv/bin/python3 lacks huggingface_hub+transformers (benchmark_lib.sh:682 bare 'python3'), so no inferencex_result.json is produced - a chicken-and-egg gap because the harness installs them only in run_eval, after the client has already died. Also established why attempt 2's patch was likely REVERTED: it targeted /opt/envs/vllm/.../vllm, but the server runs from /opt/envs/wu1w via VLLM_BIN, so such a patch is inert; and an env fix pinning HIP to a same-length physical id passes torch's length check yet yields is_available()==False.
